Caprese Salad

Classic Caprese salad with buffalo mozzarella, ripe tomatoes, basil, and extra-virgin olive oil.

title: Insalata di Rinforzo
instructions:
Insalata di Rinforzo

Neapolitan cauliflower salad with papaccelle peppers, pickled vegetables, olives, anchovies, and capers dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 large cauliflower, about 7 cups florets
5 pickled papaccelle peppers
about 1 2/3 cups mixed pickled vegetables
about 1 cup pitted green olives
about 1 cup pitted Gaeta black olives
10 salt-packed anchovies, rinsed and filleted
1/3 cup rinsed capers
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tbsp white-wine vinegar
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Remove the leaves and tough base from the cauliflower.

2. Divide into even florets.

3. Bring plenty of water to a boil with half of the salt.

4. Boil the cauliflower for about 8–10 minutes, keeping it slightly firm.

5. Drain.

6. Cool completely.

7. Drain the pickled vegetables thoroughly.

8. Cut the anchovies into pieces.

9. Cut the papaccelle into strips after removing the stems and seeds.

10. Combine the cauliflower, pickled vegetables, olives, anchovies, capers, and papaccelle in a large salad bowl.

11. Whisk together the olive oil, vinegar, remaining salt, and pepper.

12. Pour the dressing over the salad.

13. Toss gently.

14. Cover.

15. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Service

Remove from the refrigerator 15 minutes before serving and toss gently.

Chef's note

Keep the cauliflower slightly crisp; overcooked florets break apart during the long rest in the dressing.

title: Neapolitan Octopus Salad
instructions:
Neapolitan Octopus Salad

Neapolitan octopus salad with celery, pickled vegetables, garlic, parsley, lemon, and vinegar.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 large octopuses, about 2 1/4 lb each
2 large celery stalks, cut into pieces
2 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
juice of 1 lemon
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp white-wine vinegar
about 1 2/3 cups drained julienned pickled vegetables
1 1/3 tsp coarse herb salt or coarse salt
1 tsp ground white pepper
2 lemons, cut into wedges
1 cup mayonnaise for serving

Preparation

1. Clean the octopuses, removing the eyes and beaks.

2. Rinse very thoroughly.

3. Bring a large pot of water to a gentle boil with the coarse salt.

4. Add the octopuses.

5. Cook over low heat until tender, about 45–60 minutes.

6. Check by inserting a fork into the thickest part of a tentacle.

7. Remove the octopuses from the water.

8. While still warm, cut into pieces about 1 1/4 inches wide.

9. Arrange in a large serving dish.

10. Add the pickled vegetables and celery.

11. Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, and white pepper.

13. Add the garlic and parsley.

14. Toss thoroughly.

15. Cover.

16. Refrigerate for about 30 minutes.

Chef's note

Dressing the octopus while still warm helps the meat absorb the aromatic dressing more effectively.

title: Procida Lemon Salad
instructions:
Procida Lemon Salad

Procida bread-lemon salad with onion, garlic, mint, chile, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 2 servings

Ingredients

1 large Procida bread lemon
1/2 onion, very thinly sliced
1 garlic clove
about 1/2 cup fresh mint leaves
1 fresh chile
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 tsp fine salt
2 slices toasted bread, optional for serving

Preparation

1. Wash the lemon very thoroughly.

2. Remove only the thin bitter yellow outer peel, leaving plenty of the thick white pith.

3. Cut the lemon into coarse pieces.

4. Slice the onion very thinly.

5. Put the mint, garlic, half of the chile, 1 tablespoon olive oil, and salt in a mortar.

6. Pound for about 2 minutes into an aromatic paste.

7. Add the lemon pieces.

8. Crush gently for 2–3 minutes, just enough to release some juice without turning the white pith into mush.

9. Add the onion.

10. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil.

11. Toss gently.

12. Rest for 10 minutes.

Service

Serve cool but not ice-cold, with toast if desired, and finish with the remaining chile.

Chef's note

The Procida bread lemon is essential because its thick white pith is mild and edible; an ordinary juice lemon would be considerably more acidic.

title: Cialledda
instructions:
Cialledda

Cold Puglian bread salad with stale bread, cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, oregano, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 7 cups stale rustic bread cubes
1 cup cherry tomatoes
2 small cucumbers
1 small red onion
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp dried oregano
3/4 tsp fine salt
2/3 cup cold water

Preparation

1. Thinly slice the onion.

2. Soak it in cold water for 10 minutes.

3. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

4. Put them in a bowl.

5. Season with 1 tablespoon olive oil, half of the salt, and 1 teaspoon oregano.

6. Rest for 10–15 minutes.

7. Cut the bread into large cubes.

8. Drain and dry the onion.

9. Peel the cucumbers.

10. Slice them thinly.

11. Combine the bread, cucumbers, onion, and tomatoes with all of their juices.

12. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil, the remaining salt, and 1/2 teaspoon oregano.

13. Toss gently.

14. Add about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon cold water first.

15. Let it absorb for 5 minutes.

16. Add the remaining water only if the bread is still too dry.

17. Finish with the remaining olive oil and oregano.

Service

Rest until the liquid is absorbed and serve cool.

Chef's note

Adding the water in two stages prevents very porous stale bread from becoming mushy.

title: Acquasale
instructions:
Acquasale

Salento stale-bread salad with tomatoes, onion, oregano, water, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

10 slices stale rustic bread
2 2/3 cups chopped ripe red tomatoes
1 onion, thinly sliced
1/2 cup water
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Arrange the bread slices in a wide shallow dish.

2. Slowly pour the water over the bread.

3. Rest for no more than 20 minutes.

4. Check that the crumb has softened while the crust still has structure.

5. Gently squeeze the bread.

6. Cut into pieces.

7. Transfer to a salad bowl.

8. Dice the tomatoes, saving all of their juice.

9. Add them to the bread.

10. Add the onion.

11. Season with the olive oil, oregano, and salt.

12. Toss gently.

13. Cover.

14. Refrigerate for about 30 minutes.

Service

Remove from the refrigerator 10 minutes before serving.

Chef's note

The bread should absorb water without becoming soggy; limiting the soak to 20 minutes preserves the crust's structure.

Orange and Fennel Salad

Sicilian orange-and-fennel salad with anchovies, black olives, red onion, and orange dressing.

Dress only shortly before serving to keep the fennel crisp and prevent the orange acid from softening it too much.

instructions:
Pantesca Salad

Pantelleria salad with potatoes, cherry tomatoes, marinated onion, olives, capers, oregano, basil, and thyme.

2 onions

3. Add half of the salt.

5. Drain.

6. Peel while still warm.

8. Thinly slice the onions.

9. Put them in the vinegar.

10. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.

11. Rinse the capers thoroughly.

12. Soak them in cold water for 15 minutes.

13. Drain and dry.

14. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

15. Drain the onions.

16. Combine the potatoes, tomatoes, onions, olives, and capers in a bowl.

17. Add torn lettuce if using.

18. Add the oregano, basil, and thyme.

19. Dress with the olive oil and remaining salt.

20. Toss gently.

Chef's note

Marinating the onion in vinegar softens its sharpness while preserving the crisp texture the salad needs.

instructions:
Sicilian Octopus Salad

Sicilian octopus salad with tomatoes, radishes, bell pepper, celery, olives, garlic, parsley, and oregano.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 cleaned octopus, about 2 1/4 lb
1 2/3 cups chopped tomatoes

about 3/4 cup sliced celery
about 1/2 cup pitted green olives

1 tsp dried oregano
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 tbsp lemon juice, divided
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 bay leaf and 1 celery stalk for cooking, optional

Preparation

1. Bring plenty of unsalted water to a boil.

2. Add the bay leaf and celery if using.

3. Dip the octopus tentacles into the boiling water 2–3 times to curl them.

4. Lower the whole octopus into the water.

5. Reduce the heat.

6. Simmer gently for 35–50 minutes, depending on size.

7. Turn off the heat.

8. Rest the octopus in its cooking liquid for 20–30 minutes.

9. Drain.

10. Cut into pieces 3/4–1 1/4 inches wide.

11. Prepare the tomatoes, radishes, bell pepper, and celery.

12. Whisk about 3 tbsp plus 1 tsp olive oil with 1 tbsp plus 2 tsp lemon juice, the salt, and pepper.

13. Combine the octopus, vegetables, olives, garlic, parsley, and oregano in a bowl.

14. Add the dressing.

15. Toss gently.

16. Cover.

Resting the octopus in its cooking liquid after simmering helps keep it tender and juicy.

instructions:
Green Bean, Potato, and Tomato Salad

Sicilian salad of green beans, potatoes, tomatoes, and Giarratana onion with basil and oregano.

title: Olbia-style Octopus Salad
instructions:
Olbia-style Octopus Salad

Olbia-style octopus dressed with warm aromatic olive oil, garlic, parsley, chile, vinegar, and lemon.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

1 whole fresh octopus, about 4 1/2 lb
1 bay leaf
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp wine vinegar for cooking
1/2 cup water
1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil
2 garlic cloves, minced
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 fresh chile, minced
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp wine vinegar for the dressing
2 tbsp lemon juice
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Clean and rinse the octopus thoroughly.

2. Put it in a pot with the water, bay leaf, and cooking vinegar.

3. Cover.

4. Bring to a gentle simmer.

5. Cook for about 20 minutes for a very small tender octopus; for a 4 1/2-pound octopus, continue until a fork enters the thickest part of a tentacle easily, usually 35–50 minutes.

6. Turn off the heat.

7. Cool the octopus in its own cooking liquid.

8. Drain.

9. Remove any loose surface residue.

10. Cut into even pieces.

11. Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat.

12. Add the garlic, parsley, and chile.

13. Cook for 1–2 minutes without burning the garlic.

14. Add the dressing vinegar.

15. Immediately remove from the heat.

16. Pour the warm dressing over the octopus.

17. Add the lemon juice and salt.

18. Mix well.

19. Cover.

20. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Service

Remove from the refrigerator 15 minutes before serving.

Chef's note

Cooling the octopus in its own cooking liquid limits moisture loss and helps keep it tender.

instructions:
Tuscan Farro Salad

Tuscan farro salad with green beans, cherry tomatoes, Taggiasca olives, mint, basil, oregano, and lemon.

about 2 cups green beans

1/4 cup torn fresh basil
2 tsp dried oregano
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided

Preparation

1. Trim the green beans.

2. Bring plenty of water to a boil with about 1/2 teaspoon salt.

3. Boil the green beans for about 10 minutes.

4. Drain.

5. Cool immediately in cold water.

6. Dry and cut into pieces.

7. Cook the farro according to the package directions in lightly salted water.

8. Drain very thoroughly.

9. Transfer the still-warm farro to a large bowl.

10. Dress with 2 tablespoons olive oil, half of the basil, and half of the mint.

11. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

12. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet.

13. Add the tomatoes.

14. Season with the oregano, pepper, and about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

15. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.

16. Cool slightly.

17. Add the green beans, tomatoes, and olives to the farro.

18. Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice and remaining salt.

19. Pour over the salad.

20. Add the remaining herbs.

21. Toss gently.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Dressing the farro while still warm helps the grains absorb the olive oil and fresh-herb aromas more effectively.

Roman mixed wild greens blanched and sautéed with garlic, chile, and olive oil.

13. Drain the giardiniera.

title: Alba-style Raw Beef Salad
instructions:
Alba-style Raw Beef Salad

Lean Fassona beef finely chopped by hand and dressed with lemon, garlic, olive oil, salt, and pepper.

about 2 cups fresh Caesar's mushrooms or about 3/4 cup thinly shaved truffle, optional and only in season

Preparation

1. Keep the beef, knife, and cutting board very cold.

2. Remove all fat, membrane, and connective tissue from the beef.

3. Cut the beef first into thin slices.

4. Cut into narrow strips.

5. Chop finely by hand without turning it into a paste.

19. Arrange it on plates.

20. Add the whole beans and bean purée.

The hot guanciale dressing lightly wilts the radicchio without fully cooking it.

title: Tiramisù
instructions:
Tiramisù

Traditional Treviso tiramisù with mascarpone cream, ladyfingers, coffee, and cocoa.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

1 1/4 cups mascarpone
3 egg yolks or 1/4 cup pasteurized egg yolk
7 tbsp granulated sugar
about 24 ladyfingers
1 1/4 cups moka coffee, cooled
2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder

Preparation

1. Prepare the coffee.

2. Cool completely.

3. Put the egg yolks and sugar in a bowl.

4. Beat until pale and fluffy and the sugar is almost completely dissolved.

5. Gradually add the mascarpone.

6. Mix gently until smooth and uniform.

7. Pour the cold coffee into a shallow dish.

8. Quickly dip the ladyfingers one at a time without soaking them excessively.

9. Arrange a compact layer of dipped ladyfingers in the bottom of a baking dish.

10. Cover with half of the mascarpone cream.

11. Add a second layer of dipped ladyfingers.

12. Cover with the remaining cream.

13. Smooth the surface.

14. Cover.

15. Refrigerate for at least 10 hours, preferably overnight.

16. Sift the cocoa over the top immediately before serving.

Service

Serve well chilled.

Chef's note

The long rest is essential because it lets the ladyfingers absorb moisture from the cream and allows the dessert to set without becoming soggy.

instructions:
Panna Cotta

Piedmont vanilla panna cotta made with fresh cream, sugar, and gelatin.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 cups plus 2 tbsp heavy cream
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
1 vanilla bean
4 gelatin sheets, or about 2 1/2 tsp powdered gelatin equivalent

Preparation

1. Soak the gelatin sheets in abundant cold water.

2. Let soften for 10–15 minutes.

3. Split the vanilla bean lengthwise.

4. Scrape out the seeds.

5. Put the cream, sugar, vanilla seeds, and pod in a saucepan.

6. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring, without boiling.

7. Once the sugar is fully dissolved and the cream is very hot, remove from the heat.

8. Remove the vanilla pod.

9. Squeeze the gelatin sheets thoroughly.

10. Add them to the hot cream.

11. Stir until completely dissolved.

12. Divide among 4 molds holding about 2/3 cup each.

13. Cool slightly.

14. Cover.

15. Refrigerate for at least 5 hours.

16. To unmold, dip the bottom of each mold in very hot water for 2–3 seconds.

17. Invert onto a plate.

Service

Serve cold, plain or with fruit or sauce as desired.

Chef's note

Do not boil the cream because excessive heat can affect both aroma and texture.

title: Bonèt
instructions:
Bonèt

Piedmont cocoa custard with amaretti, ladyfingers, coffee, and rum, baked in a water bath.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups whole milk
about 10–12 ladyfingers, finely crumbled
about 1 1/2 cups small dry amaretti cookies, finely crumbled
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
1 cup granulated sugar, divided
1/4 cup espresso
1 tbsp ground coffee
2 tbsp rum
5 large eggs

Preparation

1. Heat the milk until almost boiling.

2. Remove from the heat.

3. Cool until warm.

4. Finely crumble the ladyfingers and amaretti.

5. Add them to the milk.

6. Add the espresso, ground coffee, and rum.

7. Stir.

8. Put 3/4 cup of the sugar in a bowl with the cocoa and eggs.

9. Whisk until uniform and lightly foamy.

10. Gradually incorporate the milk-and-cookie mixture.

11. Put the remaining 1/4 cup sugar in a small saucepan.

12. Heat over medium heat without stirring until amber caramel forms.

13. Immediately coat the bottom and sides of a pudding mold with the caramel.

14. Pour in the bonèt mixture.

15. Set the mold in a deep roasting pan.

16. Add hot water to reach halfway up the sides of the mold.

17. Bake in a preheated 340°F oven for 35–40 minutes, until the center is set but still slightly trembling.

18. Remove from the water bath.

19. Cool completely.

20. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

21. Run a thin knife around the edge.

22. Invert onto a serving platter.

Service

Serve cold.

Chef's note

Bonèt should set gently in a water bath; aggressive heat creates a grainy texture.

Baci di Dama

15. Bake for 15–18 minutes.

17. Melt the chocolate over a water bath.

18. Put a small amount of chocolate on the flat side of half of the cookies.

19. Sandwich with the remaining cookies.

Grinding the nuts with some of the sugar helps prevent them from turning into an oily paste.

title: Gianduiotti

Gianduiotti

Turin chocolates made with Piedmont hazelnuts, dark chocolate, powdered sugar, and cocoa butter.

Yield: about 30 pieces

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups toasted peeled hazelnuts
about 1 cup finely chopped 70% dark chocolate
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp powdered sugar
1/3 cup cocoa-butter wafers
1 pinch fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the hazelnuts and powdered sugar in a food processor.

2. Process for several minutes, stopping occasionally to scrape the sides.

3. Continue until the hazelnuts release their oil and form a very smooth paste.

4. Finely chop the chocolate.

5. Put it with the cocoa butter in a heatproof bowl.

6. Melt over a water bath to about 113°F.

7. Remove from the heat.

8. Mix in the hazelnut paste and salt.

9. Stir until completely uniform.

10. Cool the mixture while stirring to 82–84°F.

11. Gently rewarm to about 88°F.

12. Pour into traditional boat-shaped molds.

13. Tap the mold lightly on the counter to release air bubbles.

14. Let crystallize at room temperature for at least 1 hour.

15. Unmold gently.

Service

Store and serve at cool room temperature.

Chef's note

A perfectly smooth hazelnut paste is essential for the melting texture of traditional gianduiotti.

2. Wash and dry the peaches.

3. Cut them in half without peeling.

4. Remove the pits.

5. Scoop out a small amount of flesh, leaving about a 3/8-inch border.

6. Reserve the removed peach flesh.

7. Finely crush the amaretti.

8. Put the amaretti, peach flesh, cocoa, egg yolks, sugar, and rum in a food processor.

9. Blend until uniform.

10. Butter a baking dish with half of the butter.

14. Bake for about 1 hour.

15. Cool slightly.

title: Langhe Hazelnut Cake

Langhe Hazelnut Cake

Flourless Piedmont cake made with toasted hazelnuts, eggs, and sugar.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

4 large eggs
1 1/2 cups toasted hazelnuts
1 cup granulated sugar
1 pinch fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Line the bottom of a 9-inch cake pan with parchment.

3. Finely grind the hazelnuts without turning them into nut butter.

4. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

5. Put the whites in a perfectly clean bowl.

6. Add the salt.

7. Beat to stiff peaks.

8. In another bowl, beat the yolks with the sugar for 4–5 minutes, until pale and fluffy.

9. Mix in the ground hazelnuts.

10. Fold in one-third of the beaten whites to lighten the mixture.

11. Gently fold in the remaining whites in two additions.

12. Pour into the pan.

13. Smooth gently.

14. Bake for 30–35 minutes.

15. Test with a toothpick.

16. Cool completely before unmolding.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Gentle folding is essential because, without flour, the whipped egg whites provide the cake's lift and structure.

Zabaglione

Piedmont zabaglione whipped over a water bath with Moscato d'Asti.

Yield: 10 servings

Ingredients

10 egg yolks
1/2 cup plus 1 1/2 tbsp granulated sugar
2/3 cup Moscato d'Asti

Preparation

1. Prepare a water bath with hot water that is not boiling vigorously.

2. Put the egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl.

3. Whisk for 4–5 minutes, until pale and foamy.

4. Gradually add the Moscato d'Asti while continuing to whisk.

5. Set the bowl over the water bath without letting its bottom touch the water.

6. Whisk constantly.

7. Cook gently until the zabaglione increases in volume, becomes foamy, and is thick enough for the whisk to leave a visible trail, about 8–12 minutes.

8. Remove immediately from the heat.

9. Whisk for another 30 seconds to even out the temperature.

Service

Chef's note

Keep the water bath gentle because excessive heat coagulates the yolks and makes the zabaglione grainy.

Tegole Valdostane

Thin crisp Valle d'Aosta cookies made with hazelnuts, almonds, butter, and vanilla.

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Lightly toast the hazelnuts and almonds for 6–8 minutes.

5. Process the sugar, hazelnuts, and almonds until very finely ground.

6. Transfer to a bowl.

7. Add the egg whites.

8. Melt the butter and cool slightly.

9. Mix in the melted butter.

10. Add the flour and vanilla seeds.

11. Mix until uniform.

12. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

Tegole become rigid within seconds of leaving the oven, so shape them immediately while still flexible.

Preparation

2. Let soften for 10 minutes.

3. Split the vanilla bean.

5. Pour the cream into a saucepan.

6. Add the sugar, vanilla seeds, and pod.

7. Heat slowly while stirring.

8. Stop just before the cream boils.

9. Remove from the heat.

10. Remove the vanilla pod.

11. Squeeze the gelatin thoroughly.

12. Add it to the hot cream.

13. Stir until completely dissolved.

14. Divide among 6 molds.

15. Cool slightly.

16. Cover.

Chef's note

The cream should be very hot but not boiling so the gelatin dissolves without compromising the dessert's delicate texture.

Mecoulin

Cogne sweet bread with raisins, rum, cream, butter, olive oil, and lemon zest.

Yield: 1 large sweet loaf

Ingredients

1 cup whole milk, room temperature
2 cups all-purpose flour
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp heavy cream
3 large eggs
1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
2/3 cup raisins
2 tbsp butter
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp olive oil
about 2 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
2 tbsp rum
finely grated zest of 1 organic lemon
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the raisins in a bowl.

2. Add the rum.

3. Soak for about 2 hours.

4. Dissolve the yeast and 1 tablespoon of the sugar in 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon milk.

5. Put about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour in a bowl.

6. Add the yeast milk.

7. Mix into a soft starter.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for about 1 hour.

10. Put the remaining flour in a large bowl.

11. Add the starter.

12. Add the remaining milk, olive oil, softened butter, cream, 2 beaten eggs, lemon zest, salt, and remaining sugar.

13. Knead until smooth and elastic.

14. Cover.

15. Let rise until doubled.

16. Work in the raisins and any unabsorbed rum.

17. Shape into a round loaf.

18. Put on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Let rise for another hour.

21. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

22. Beat the remaining egg.

23. Brush the top.

24. Bake for about 60 minutes.

25. Test with a skewer.

26. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Slice and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Add the raisins only after the first full rise so they do not weigh down the dough during its early development.

instructions:
Crema di Cogne

Valle d'Aosta gianduia cream with nut-infused milk, cream, and crisp hazelnut wafers.

Yield: about 4 servings

Ingredients

For the cream
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp whole milk
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp heavy cream

2 large egg yolks

3 tbsp almonds

For the wafers
about 1/4 cup egg whites
3 1/2 tbsp melted butter
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
1/2 cup hazelnut flour
1/4 cup granulated sugar

Preparation

1. Heat the milk to about 175°F.

2. Add the almonds and hazelnuts.

3. Cover.

4. Infuse for about 2 hours.

5. Strain the milk.

6. Heat the cream to about 185°F.

7. In a bowl, mix the yolks, sugar, cornstarch, and chopped gianduia.

8. Gradually add the hot cream.

9. Add the infused milk.

10. Transfer to a saucepan.

11. Cook, stirring constantly, to about 185°F without boiling.

12. Add the caramelized sugar.

13. Stir until fully dissolved.

14. Transfer to a bowl.

15. Cover directly on the surface.

16. Cool completely.

17. For the wafers, mix the sugar and egg whites without whipping.

18. Add the melted butter.

19. Mix in the flour and hazelnut flour.

20. Refrigerate the batter for 30 minutes.

21. Preheat the oven to 340°F.

22. Spread very thin disks on parchment.

23. Bake for about 8 minutes.

24. Immediately curve the hot wafers over a rounded surface.

Service

Spoon the cold cream into dishes and serve with the crisp wafers.

Chef's note

Do not let the cream boil; gentle cooking keeps the yolks and gianduia smooth.

Pandolce Genovese

Traditional tall Genoese sweet bread with raisins, pine nuts, candied citron, fennel seeds, and orange-flower water.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

6 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast

2 cups raisins
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp pine nuts

1. The night before, dissolve the yeast in about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon warm water taken from the total liquid.

2. Add 2 1/2 cups flour.

3. Knead into a soft starter.

4. Put in a bowl.

5. Cover.

6. Let rise in a warm place overnight.

7. The next day, soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

8. Drain and dry thoroughly.

9. Chop the candied citron.

10. Melt the butter.

11. Cool slightly.

12. Put the remaining flour in a large bowl.

13. Add the starter, butter, remaining water-and-orange-flower mixture, sugar, and salt.

14. Knead vigorously for 10 minutes.

15. Add the raisins, citron, pine nuts, and fennel seeds.

16. Knead for another 5 minutes.

17. Divide the dough in half.

18. Shape two round loaves.

19. Put them on a buttered or parchment-lined baking sheet.

20. Cover.

21. Let rise for about 12 hours.

22. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

23. Cut a triangular slash into the top of each loaf.

24. Bake for about 40 minutes.

25. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Slice and serve at room temperature.

The two very long rises develop the characteristic aroma of traditional tall pandolce.

instructions:
Sacripantina

Genoese layered sponge cake with Marsala-rum cream, cocoa cream, and a hidden canestrello cookie in the center.

Yield: 10 servings

Ingredients

For the sponge cake
5 medium eggs
2/3 cup all-purpose flour
2/3 cup potato starch

1 packet vanilla sugar or 1 tsp vanilla extract
1 pinch fine salt

For the creams
3 egg yolks
2/3 cup granulated sugar
6 tbsp potato starch
1 1/2 cups whole milk
1 cup plus 1 tbsp softened butter
3 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp Marsala
2 tbsp rum

For the soaking syrup
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp rum
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp Marsala
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp water
1 tbsp granulated sugar

For the center
1 canestrello cookie

For finishing
1/4 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 320°F.

2. Beat the 5 eggs with the vanilla and salt.

3. Gradually add the sugar.

4. Continue beating until very pale and voluminous.

5. Sift the flour and potato starch.

6. Fold them in gently.

7. Pour into a 9 1/2-inch round pan lined on the bottom with parchment.

8. Bake for about 50 minutes.

9. Cool completely.

10. For the pastry cream, heat the milk.

11. Beat the 3 yolks with the sugar.

12. Add the potato starch.

13. Add the Marsala.

14. Gradually add the hot milk.

15. Return to low heat.

16. Cook, stirring, until thick.

17. Transfer to a bowl.

18. Cool completely, stirring occasionally.

19. Beat the softened butter until creamy.

20. Add 1 tablespoon rum.

21. Gradually beat in the cooled pastry cream.

22. Remove about one-third of the cream.

23. Mix the cocoa and remaining rum into that portion.

24. For the syrup, dissolve the sugar in the water.

25. Cool.

26. Add the rum and Marsala.

27. Level the sponge cake, saving all crumbs.

28. Cut horizontally into 3 disks.

29. Moisten the first disk with syrup.

30. Spread with cocoa cream, forming a slight dome.

31. Moisten the canestrello with a little Marsala.

32. Put it in the center with 1 tablespoon plain cream.

33. Cover with the second cake disk.

34. Moisten with syrup.

35. Add plain cream.

36. Cover with the final disk.

37. Moisten lightly.

38. Cover the entire cake with the remaining cream.

39. Coat with the reserved sponge crumbs.

40. Refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

41. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Service

Serve cold.

Chef's note

The pastry cream and butter should be at the same temperature before combining or the cream can split.

instructions:
Amaretti di Sassello

Soft Sassello amaretti made with almonds, egg whites, sugar, and vanilla.

Yield: about 30 cookies

Ingredients

1 1/4 cups ground almonds
2 cups powdered sugar
1/2 cup plus 1 tbsp granulated sugar
4 egg whites
1/2 tsp vanilla extract

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Process the almonds for about 1 minute.

3. Add the powdered sugar.

4. Process for another 2 minutes.

5. Sift the mixture into a bowl.

6. Put the egg whites in a perfectly clean bowl.

7. Beat to soft peaks.

8. Gradually add the granulated sugar.

9. Continue beating until glossy.

10. Add the vanilla.

11. Gently fold in the almond-and-powdered-sugar mixture.

12. Transfer to a pastry bag fitted with a plain 3/8-inch tip.

13. Pipe disks about 1 inch wide onto a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Rest for about 15 minutes.

15. Bake for about 15 minutes.

16. Cool completely on the baking sheet.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Fold in the almond mixture gently so the egg whites do not deflate excessively and the amaretti remain soft.

title: Gobeletti
instructions:
Gobeletti

Genoese shortcrust tartlets filled with jam and dusted with powdered sugar.

Yield: about 12–16 pieces

Ingredients

2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
14 tbsp cold butter
1/2 cup granulated sugar
1 egg yolk
about 2/3 cup jam
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Put the flour and sugar in a bowl.

2. Add the cold diced butter.

3. Work quickly until sandy.

4. Add the egg yolk.

5. Mix briefly into a uniform dough.

6. Wrap.

7. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

8. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

9. Roll the dough about 3/16 inch thick, not too thin.

10. Cut fluted disks about 3 inches wide.

11. Line the traditional concave molds with half of the disks.

12. Put about 1 tablespoon jam in each mold.

13. Cover with a second disk.

14. Seal the edges carefully.

15. Bake for about 20 minutes, until golden.

16. Cool completely.

17. Unmold.

18. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Do not roll the pastry too thin; it must support the jam without breaking during unmolding.

title: Ligurian Castagnaccio
instructions:
Ligurian Castagnaccio

Ligurian chestnut-flour cake with raisins, pine nuts, and rosemary.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

2 cups chestnut flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
1/4 cup granulated sugar
1/4 cup raisins
3 tbsp pine nuts
1 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary
2 tbsp olive oil
1/2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry.

3. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

4. Sift the chestnut flour into a bowl.

5. Gradually whisk in the water.

6. Continue until smooth and free of lumps.

7. Add the sugar and salt.

8. Grease an 8 1/2-inch pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

9. Pour in the batter.

10. Scatter the raisins and pine nuts over the top.

11. Add the rosemary.

12. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

13. Bake for about 50 minutes.

14. Remove when the surface is dry and lightly cracked.

15. Cool slightly.

Service

Cut into portions and serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The batter should be fluid and lump-free; adding the water gradually makes the consistency easier to control.

title: Panera Genovese
instructions:
Panera Genovese

Genoese coffee semifreddo with ricotta, whipped cream, and meringue.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

1 cup ricotta
1 2/3 cups heavy cream
4 large eggs, separated
1/2 cup granulated sugar
2 tsp decaffeinated instant coffee

Preparation

1. Line a 9 1/2-inch loaf pan with plastic wrap, leaving an overhang on all sides.

2. Separate the egg yolks and whites.

3. Put the yolks in a bowl.

4. Add the instant coffee.

5. Stir until the coffee is fully dissolved.

6. Work the ricotta with a spatula until smooth.

7. Mix it into the yolk-and-coffee mixture.

8. Whip the cold cream to firm peaks without overwhipping.

9. In a second bowl, begin beating the egg whites.

10. Once foamy, gradually add the sugar.

11. Continue beating until glossy and firm.

12. Gently fold the ricotta-and-coffee mixture into the whipped cream.

13. Add the beaten egg whites in several additions.

14. Fold gently to preserve as much air as possible.

15. Pour into the prepared pan.

16. Smooth the surface.

17. Cover with the overhanging plastic wrap.

18. Freeze for about 6 hours, until completely firm.

19. Remove from the freezer 10 minutes before serving.

20. Unmold and remove the plastic wrap.

Service

Cut into thick slices and serve immediately.

Chef's note

Gentle folding preserves the air in the whipped cream and egg whites and gives the semifreddo a light, even texture.

title: Ligurian Sweet Rice Cake
instructions:
Ligurian Sweet Rice Cake

Liguria rice-and-milk cake with eggs, vanilla, and lemon zest.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

2/3 cup Originario or other short-grain rice
3 1/2 cups whole milk
1 1/2 tbsp butter, plus more for the pan
6 large eggs
3/4 cup granulated sugar
finely grated zest of 1 untreated lemon
1 vanilla bean
1 tbsp granulated sugar for finishing
1 pinch fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the rice in a saucepan.

2. Add the milk.

3. Add a pinch of salt.

4. Bring slowly to a boil.

5. Reduce the heat.

6. Cook, stirring often, until the rice is tender and most of the milk has been absorbed.

7. Remove from the heat.

8. Stir in the butter.

9. Cool until warm.

10. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

11. Butter a 10-inch cake pan.

12. Split the vanilla bean.

13. Scrape out the seeds.

14. Beat the eggs and sugar in a large bowl.

15. Add the lemon zest and vanilla seeds.

16. Stir in the rice-and-milk mixture.

17. Mix until uniform.

18. Pour into the pan.

19. Bake for about 50 minutes.

20. If the top browns too quickly, loosely cover with foil during the final minutes.

21. Remove from the oven.

22. Sprinkle the top with the tablespoon of sugar.

23. Broil for 2–3 minutes, until lightly caramelized.

24. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature or slightly cool.

Chef's note

Cooling the rice mixture before adding it to the eggs prevents the eggs from curdling.

title: Milanese Panettone
instructions:
Milanese Panettone

Traditional long-fermented Milanese panettone with raisins, candied citron, and candied orange.

Yield: 3 loaves, about 2 1/4 lb each

Ingredients

about 2 cups fermented bread dough
about 11 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, divided
1 3/4 cups butter, plus more for finishing
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
15 large eggs
1 1/3 cups raisins
1/3 cup diced candied citron
1/3 cup diced candied orange peel
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
about 1 2/3 cups warm water, divided as needed

Preparation

1. Put the fermented dough in a large bowl.

2. Add 1 1/4 cups flour.

3. Add 1/3–scant 1/2 cup warm water.

4. Knead into a soft elastic dough.

5. Shape into a ball.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise in a warm place for at least 3 hours.

8. Return the dough to the work surface.

9. Add 1 cup flour and about 1/4–1/3 cup warm water.

10. Knead again.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise for about 2 hours.

13. Soak the raisins in warm water for 20 minutes.

14. Drain.

15. Dry thoroughly.

16. Finely dice the candied citron and orange peel.

17. Melt 1 1/2 cups butter.

18. Cool until warm.

19. Separate 10 eggs, reserving the yolks.

20. Keep the remaining 5 eggs whole.

21. Put the sugar and 1/2 cup water in a saucepan.

22. Heat until a clear syrup forms.

23. Cool until warm.

24. Put about 8 1/3 cups flour in a large mixer bowl or on a work surface.

25. Add the salt.

26. Add the fermented dough.

27. Gradually incorporate the melted butter and syrup.

28. Slowly add the 10 yolks and 5 whole eggs.

29. Knead for about 20 minutes, adding only enough additional warm water to make a soft but elastic dough.

30. Work in the raisins and candied fruit.

31. Divide the dough into 3 equal portions.

32. Round each portion into a smooth ball.

33. Put each piece into a 2 1/4-lb panettone mold.

34. Cover.

35. Let rise for about 6 hours, until the dough approaches the top of the molds.

36. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

37. Cut a cross into the top of each loaf.

38. Put a small piece of the remaining butter in the center of each cross.

39. Bake for 5 minutes at 400°F.

40. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

41. Continue baking for 55–75 minutes, until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.

42. Loosely cover with foil if the tops brown too quickly.

43. Remove from the oven.

44. Pierce the base of each panettone with panettone skewers or sturdy metal rods.

45. Immediately invert.

46. Cool suspended upside down for at least 6 hours.

Service

Serve at room temperature after completely cooling.

Chef's note

Cooling upside down prevents the butter-and-egg-rich crumb from collapsing.

title: Colomba Pasquale
instructions:
Colomba Pasquale

Long-fermented Easter dove bread with candied orange and almond glaze.

Yield: about 3 loaves, 2 1/4 lb each

Ingredients

First dough
6 2/3 cups strong bread flour
1 1/3 cups softened butter
about 2/3 cup egg yolks
1 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
about 1 1/2 cups active sourdough starter
1 3/4 cups water

Second dough
1 2/3 cups strong bread flour
1 1/3 cups softened butter
about 1 cup egg yolks
1 cup granulated sugar
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp acacia honey
about 5 1/3 cups diced candied orange peel
1/2 tsp colomba or citrus-vanilla flavoring
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

For the glaze
1 cup almond flour
1/2 cup egg whites
1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
3 tbsp toasted hazelnuts
1/2 cup whole blanched almonds
1 tbsp bitter almonds

Preparation

1. Put the first-dough flour, sugar, water, and active starter in a mixer bowl.

2. Mix for 15 minutes, until the dough begins developing strength.

3. Gradually add the egg yolks.

4. Once absorbed, add the softened butter a little at a time.

5. Continue mixing until smooth, elastic, and fully developed.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise for 10–12 hours at about 75°F, until tripled.

8. Return the first dough to the mixer.

9. Add the second-dough flour.

10. Mix for 15 minutes.

11. Gradually add the sugar.

12. Add the egg yolks little by little.

13. Add the softened butter.

14. Add the honey, salt, and flavoring.

15. Finally work in the candied orange.

16. Continue mixing until fully developed and elastic, about 45–50 minutes total for the second dough.

17. Rest for 60 minutes.

18. Divide into portions sized for 2 1/4-lb molds.

19. Round each portion.

20. Rest for 20 minutes.

21. Divide and shape pieces for the body and wings.

22. Arrange in the dove molds.

23. Proof for 5–6 hours at 82–86°F, until the dough approaches the rim.

24. For the glaze, process the almond flour, hazelnuts, bitter almonds, and sugar.

25. Gradually add the egg whites until thick and spreadable.

26. Spread the glaze gently over the loaves.

27. Decorate with the whole almonds.

28. Preheat a convection oven to 350°F.

29. Bake 2 1/4-lb loaves for about 55 minutes.

30. Check that the center reaches about 201°F.

31. Remove from the oven.

32. Pierce each loaf near the base with sturdy skewers.

33. Immediately invert.

34. Cool suspended upside down for at least 6 hours.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Upside-down cooling is essential to support the rich, airy crumb while it sets.

title: Torta Sbrisolona
instructions:
Torta Sbrisolona

Mantua crumb cake made with wheat flour, fine corn flour, almonds, butter, and egg yolks.

Yield: 1 cake, 8 servings

Ingredients

1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups fine corn flour
14 tbsp cold butter, or 7 tbsp butter plus 7 tbsp lard
3/4 cup plus 2 tbsp granulated sugar
2/3 cup blanched almonds
2/3 cup skin-on almonds
2 egg yolks
1 vanilla bean
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Coarsely chop the blanched almonds and most of the skin-on almonds.

3. Reserve 10–15 whole almonds for the top.

4. Mix the all-purpose flour and corn flour.

5. Add the sugar.

6. Add the chopped almonds.

7. Add the salt, vanilla seeds, and lemon zest.

8. Cut the cold butter into cubes.

9. Add it to the dry ingredients.

10. Rub with your fingertips until the mixture is sandy and irregular.

11. Add the egg yolks.

12. Mix briefly while keeping the dough crumbly; do not form a smooth ball.

13. Line a 9 1/2-inch cake pan with parchment.

14. Lightly butter the parchment.

15. Scatter the crumbly dough into the pan without compacting it too much.

16. Arrange the reserved whole almonds on top.

17. Bake for about 40 minutes, until deeply golden.

18. Cool completely in the pan.

Service

Break into pieces by hand rather than cutting into neat slices.

Chef's note

The irregular crumbly structure defines sbrisolona, so never knead the mixture into a compact dough.

title: Torta Paradiso
instructions:
Torta Paradiso

Pavia butter cake with powdered sugar, lemon zest, and potato starch.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

14 tbsp softened butter
2 cups powdered sugar
5 large egg yolks
2 large whole eggs
1 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp potato starch
3/4 tsp baking powder
finely grated zest of 1 untreated lemon
1 pinch fine salt
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter and flour an 8 1/2–9 1/2-inch cake pan.

3. Put the softened butter in a large bowl.

4. Add the powdered sugar and lemon zest.

5. Beat for 15–20 minutes, until very pale and fluffy.

6. Lightly beat the whole eggs with the egg yolks.

7. Add the egg mixture to the butter very slowly, a little at a time.

8. Allow each addition to absorb completely before adding more.

9. Add the salt.

10. Sift together the flour, potato starch, and baking powder.

11. Mix the dry ingredients in on the lowest mixer speed or fold by hand.

12. Stop as soon as the batter is uniform.

13. Pour into the pan.

14. Smooth gently.

15. Bake for 35–40 minutes.

16. Test with a toothpick.

17. Unmold immediately by inverting the cake.

18. Leave it inverted for about 15 minutes.

19. Transfer to a rack.

20. Cool for at least 40 minutes.

21. Dust with the finishing powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Adding the eggs very slowly prevents the butter emulsion from breaking and keeps the crumb fine and tender.

Brutti e Buoni

Lombardy hazelnut-and-almond meringue cookies.

about 1/2 cup egg whites
1 cup powdered sugar

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 290°F.

2. Coarsely chop the hazelnuts and almonds.

3. Put the egg whites in a perfectly clean bowl.

4. Begin beating them.

5. Once foamy, gradually add the granulated sugar.

6. Continue beating until firm.

7. In a second bowl, combine the chopped nuts, powdered sugar, and vanilla.

8. Gently fold in the meringue.

9. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

10. Form irregular mounds with two spoons or a pastry bag.

11. Leave at least 1 1/4 inches between cookies.

12. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until dry and lightly golden.

13. Turn off the oven.

14. Leave the cookies inside with the door slightly open for 5 minutes.

15. Transfer to a rack.

Their intentionally rough shape is part of the identity of brutti e buoni, so do not try to make them perfectly uniform.

title: Torta Bertolina
instructions:
Torta Bertolina

Crema-area yeast cake with Concord-style strawberry grapes, corn flour, and a crisp sugar topping.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

about 4 cups stemmed strawberry grapes
1 cup fine corn flour
2 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp granulated sugar
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
1 3/4 cups water
1 pinch fine salt
2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan
2 tbsp granulated sugar for the top

Preparation

1. Wash the grapes gently.

2. Remove them from the stems.

3. Dry thoroughly.

4. Sift the all-purpose flour into a large bowl.

5. Add the corn flour.

6. Crumble in the fresh yeast.

7. Add the sugar.

8. Gradually add the water while stirring.

9. Add the salt.

10. Continue mixing until the dough is very hydrated and almost batter-like.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise for about 1 hour at 80–82°F.

13. Gently fold in the grapes without crushing them.

14. Cover again.

15. Let rise for another 45 minutes.

16. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

17. Grease a 12 1/2-inch baking pan with the olive oil.

9. Add the salt.

13. Shape into a ball.

14. Cover.

17. Add the raisins, figs, walnuts, hazelnuts, chestnuts, and pine nuts to the dough.

18. Gradually work in the reserved grappa.

19. Knead gently until the fruit is evenly distributed.

Add the fruit and nuts only after the first rise so their weight does not slow the dough's initial development.

title: Pavia Paradise Cake
instructions:
Pavia Paradise Cake

Soft Oltrepò Pavese butter cake with eggs, vanilla, lemon, and potato starch.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

14 tbsp softened butter
1 2/3 cups powdered sugar
4 egg yolks
3 large eggs
1 pinch powdered vanilla
finely grated zest of 1 untreated lemon
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp all-purpose flour

1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Butter and flour an 8 1/2–9 1/2-inch cake pan.

3. Put the softened butter in a slightly warm bowl.

4. Add the powdered sugar.

5. Beat until very pale, fluffy, and highly aerated.

6. Add the egg yolks one at a time.

7. Fully incorporate each yolk before adding the next.

8. Add the whole eggs one at a time in the same way.

9. Add the vanilla and lemon zest.

10. Sift together the flour and potato starch.

11. Fold them in gradually with a spatula.

12. Pour the batter into the pan.

13. Smooth gently.

14. Bake for about 40 minutes.

15. Test with a toothpick.

16. Cool slightly in the pan.

17. Unmold.

18. Cool completely on a rack.

19. Let the cake rest until the following day for the best texture.

20. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Service

Chef's note

Thoroughly whipping the butter and sugar at the beginning incorporates the air needed for the cake's light texture.

Bussolano Mantovano

Mantua Tagliatelle Cake

Mantua layered cake made with ultra-thin egg tagliatelle, almonds, sugar, and butter.

1 cup granulated sugar
1 1/2 cups finely chopped blanched almonds

3 egg yolks

Preparation

1. Put the flour on a work surface.

2. Make a well.

3. Add the 3 egg yolks.

4. Knead into a firm dough.

5. If the dough is too dry, add 1 tablespoon water.

6. Wrap.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Roll the pasta very thinly.

9. Let it dry for 10 minutes.

10. Cut into extremely thin tagliatelle, similar to soup noodles.

11. Mix the almonds, sugar, and about 10 1/2 tablespoons softened butter into a crumbly mixture.

12. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

13. Butter a 9 1/2-inch cake pan with the remaining butter.

14. Arrange a thin first layer of tagliatelle.

15. Scatter one-third of the almond mixture over it.

16. Repeat to make about 3 pasta layers alternating with almond mixture.

17. Finish with the almond mixture.

18. Beat the 3 whole eggs.

19. Pour slowly and evenly over the cake.

20. Bake for about 40 minutes, until golden and fully set.

21. Cool in the pan.

Chef's note

The tagliatelle must be extremely thin so they cook completely while absorbing the butter, eggs, and sugar.

title: Baicoli
instructions:
Baicoli

Venetian twice-baked yeast cookies, sliced thin and dried until crisp.

Yield: 12 servings

Ingredients

2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
1/4 cup granulated sugar
2 tbsp softened butter
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
6 tbsp warm milk
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Pour 1/4 cup warm milk into a bowl.

2. Add the yeast.

3. Add 1 teaspoon of the sugar.

4. Stir.

5. Let activate for 10 minutes.

6. Put the flour in a large bowl.

7. Add the activated yeast mixture.

8. Add the remaining sugar.

9. Add the softened butter.

10. Add the salt.

11. Knead while gradually adding the remaining 2 tablespoons milk.

12. Work until smooth and elastic.

13. Shape into a long even loaf.

14. Cover.

15. Let rise until doubled, about 1–2 hours.

16. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

17. Bake the loaf for 20–25 minutes.

18. Cool completely.

19. Preferably rest until the next day.

20. Preheat the oven to 300°F.

21. Slice the loaf extremely thinly, about 1/8 inch thick.

22. Arrange the slices in a single layer on a baking sheet.

23. Bake for 10–12 minutes.

24. Turn each slice.

25. Continue for another 8–10 minutes, until dry and golden.

26. Cool completely.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Resting between the first and second baking makes it possible to slice the loaf very thinly without breaking it.

Torta Russa di Verona

Verona cake with a puff-pastry shell and almond, amaretti, butter, and rum filling.

Yield: 12 servings

Ingredients

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter a 9 1/2-inch springform pan.

3. Roll the puff pastry into a disk about 14 inches wide.

4. Line the pan, creating a border 2 1/2–2 3/4 inches high.

5. Separate the eggs.

6. Put the softened butter in a bowl.

7. Add 1/2 cup sugar.

8. Beat until pale.

9. Add the salt and rum flavoring.

10. Add the egg yolks one at a time.

11. Mix in the almonds and amaretti.

12. Beat the egg whites to very stiff peaks.

13. Gradually add the remaining 1/4 cup sugar.

14. Spoon the whipped whites over the amaretti mixture.

15. Sift the flour over the top.

16. Fold gently.

17. Gradually add the milk.

18. Sift in and fold through the baking powder.

19. Pour the filling into the pastry-lined pan.

20. Fold the pastry border inward to form points around the top.

21. Bake on a low oven rack for 60–70 minutes.

22. Loosely cover with foil if the surface browns too quickly.

23. Cool completely.

24. Unmold.

The puff pastry should rise well above the filling before baking so it can be folded into the characteristic pointed crown.

instructions:
Pandoro di Verona

Verona laminated sweet yeast bread with butter and vanilla.

Yield: 1 loaf, about 2 1/4 lb

Ingredients

3 3/4 cups bread flour, divided
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast, divided
2/3 cup granulated sugar, divided

3 large eggs
1 egg yolk
5 tbsp warm water, divided
1 tsp fine salt
1 vanilla bean
1 tbsp butter for the mold
1 1/2 tbsp granulated sugar for the mold
1/4 cup powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. For the starter, dissolve most of the yeast in 1/4 cup warm water.

2. Add 2 teaspoons sugar.

3. Add about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour.

4. Add the egg yolk.

5. Whisk until smooth and fluid.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.

8. Dissolve the remaining yeast in 1 tablespoon warm water.

9. Add it to the starter.

10. Add 2 tablespoons sugar, 1 2/3 cups flour, and 1 egg.

11. Knead until well combined.

12. Add 2 tablespoons softened butter.

13. Work until fully absorbed.

14. Cover.

15. Let rise for about 45 minutes.

16. Add the remaining 1 2/3 cups flour, 1/2 cup sugar, 2 eggs, salt, and vanilla seeds.

17. Knead until smooth.

18. Slap and work the dough on the counter for about 10 minutes.

19. Shape into a ball.

20. Cover.

21. Rest for 30 minutes.

22. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

23. Roll into a square.

24. Flatten the remaining 10 tablespoons butter into a smaller square.

25. Put the butter in the center of the dough.

26. Fold the corners over it, sealing completely.

27. Roll gently into a rectangle.

28. Fold in thirds.

29. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.

30. Repeat the rolling, letter fold, and 20-minute chill two more times.

31. Butter a 2 1/4-lb pandoro mold.

32. Coat it with the granulated sugar.

33. Shape the dough into a smooth ball.

34. Put it in the mold seam-side up.

35. Cover.

36. Let rise until the dough approaches the rim.

37. Preheat the oven to 340°F.

38. Bake for 10 minutes.

39. Reduce the oven to 320°F.

40. Continue baking for about 45 minutes.

41. Test with a skewer.

42. Cool completely in the mold.

43. Unmold.

44. Dust with powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Cold rests between folds keep the butter distinct from the dough and create pandoro's characteristic laminated structure.

title: Fritole Veneziane

Fritole Veneziane

Venetian yeast fritters with raisins, pine nuts, grappa, and vanilla.

2. Drain.

3. Squeeze and dry thoroughly.

4. Warm half of the milk.

7. Add the yeast mixture.

8. Add the lightly beaten eggs.

12. Add the remaining milk.

13. Add the grappa, sugar, vanilla seeds, and salt.

14. Work until soft and uniform.

16. Cover.

17. Let rise in a warm place for 2–3 hours, until nearly tripled.

21. Remove with a slotted spoon.

title: Galani Veneziani
instructions:
Galani Veneziani

Ultra-thin Venetian Carnival pastries, fried and dusted with vanilla powdered sugar.

Yield: about 24 pieces

1/3 cup vanilla powdered sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Lightly beat the eggs.

2. Add the sugar, vanilla, and salt.

3. Add the melted cooled butter.

4. Add the grappa.

5. Mix.

6. Gradually add the flour.

7. Knead thoroughly until firm, smooth, and elastic.

8. Wrap in plastic.

9. Rest for 45–60 minutes.

10. Divide the dough into several pieces.

11. Run each piece through a pasta machine.

12. Gradually reduce the thickness until almost transparent.

13. Cut into long narrow rectangles.

14. Heat the oil to 350°F.

15. Fry only a few at a time for 10–20 seconds per side.

16. Turn as soon as bubbles appear and the surface reaches a pale straw color.

17. Drain immediately.

18. Transfer to paper towels.

19. Cool completely.

20. Dust with vanilla powdered sugar.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The dough must be nearly transparent before frying; that is what gives galani their exceptionally light, fragile texture.

Treviso Tiramisù

Treviso tiramisù with mascarpone cream and egg yolks pasteurized with hot sugar syrup.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

2 tbsp water
5 egg yolks
2 cups mascarpone, cold
about 30 ladyfingers
1 1/2 cups plus 1 tbsp moka coffee
3 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder

Preparation

1. Prepare the coffee.

2. Cool until warm.

3. Put the water and sugar in a small saucepan.

4. Heat the syrup to 250°F.

5. Meanwhile, begin beating the egg yolks.

6. Slowly stream the hot syrup into the yolks with the mixer running.

7. Continue beating until pale, fluffy, and cooled to room temperature.

8. Add the cold mascarpone.

9. Beat only until smooth and firm.

10. Pour the coffee into a shallow dish.

11. Quickly dip each ladyfinger on both sides without soaking it through.

12. Arrange a layer in an 8 × 12-inch dish.

13. Cover with half of the cream.

14. Sift half of the cocoa over the cream.

15. Add a second layer of dipped ladyfingers.

16. Cover with the remaining cream.

17. Sift the remaining cocoa over the top.

18. Cover with plastic wrap.

19. Refrigerate for at least 6–8 hours.

Service

Serve well chilled.

Chef's note

The 250°F sugar syrup stabilizes the cream and pasteurizes the yolks as they are whipped.

title: Gubana
instructions:
Gubana

Friulian spiral sweet bread filled with walnuts, pine nuts, almonds, raisins, grappa, and Marsala.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, divided
1/2 cup plus 2 tsp whole milk, divided
1 tsp active dry yeast
2/3 cup granulated sugar, divided
6 medium eggs, divided
9 tbsp butter, divided
2 tbsp grappa, divided
about 1/2 cup Marsala, divided
about 2 cups walnut pieces
about 1 cup pine nuts
about 1 cup raisins
1/2 cup breadcrumbs
1/2 cup blanched almonds
finely grated zest of 2 lemons
finely grated zest of 1 orange
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put about 1 1/4 cups flour in a bowl.

2. Add the yeast.

3. Add 6 tablespoons milk.

4. Knead into a uniform starter.

5. Cover.

6. Rest for at least 1 hour.

7. Put the remaining flour in a mixer bowl.

8. Add about 1/2 cup sugar.

9. Add the starter.

10. Add 3 eggs.

11. Add the zest of 1 lemon.

12. Add 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp grappa.

13. Add the remaining milk.

14. Knead.

15. Add the salt.

16. Gradually add 5 tbsp softened butter.

17. Continue until elastic.

18. Cover.

19. Let rise for at least 3 hours.

20. Soak the raisins in about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp Marsala for at least 20 minutes.

21. Coarsely chop the walnuts, almonds, and pine nuts.

22. Melt the remaining 4 tbsp butter in a skillet.

23. Add the breadcrumbs.

24. Toast for 2–3 minutes.

25. Transfer to a bowl.

26. Add the raisins and soaking Marsala.

27. Add the chopped nuts.

28. Add the remaining lemon zest and orange zest.

29. Add the remaining grappa and Marsala.

30. Separate 2 of the remaining eggs.

31. Mix the 2 yolks into the filling.

32. Beat the 2 whites.

33. Fold them gently into the filling.

34. Roll the risen dough into a large rectangle.

35. Spread the filling evenly, leaving about 3/4 inch clear around the edges.

36. Beat the final egg.

37. Brush the edges.

38. Roll tightly from a long side.

39. Coil into a spiral.

40. Put into a buttered pan.

41. Cover.

42. Let rise for 30 minutes.

43. Preheat a conventional oven to 340°F.

44. Brush with the remaining beaten egg.

45. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar.

46. Bake for about 1 hour.

47. Rest for 10 minutes.

48. Cool on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The filling should be rich but compact enough to remain evenly distributed through the spiral while baking.

title: Presnitz
instructions:
Presnitz

Trieste spiral pastry filled with nuts, raisins, candied fruit, rum, sweet wine, and spices.

Yield: 10 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 large egg
2 egg yolks
1 3/4 cups granulated sugar, divided
1 cup plus 2 tbsp butter, divided
1 pinch nutmeg
1 cup raisins
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp sweet white wine
about 1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp rum
3/4 cup almonds
about 1 1/4 cups walnuts
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp pine nuts
1/3 cup diced candied citron
1/3 cup diced candied orange peel
3 whole cloves, ground
about 3 cups grated stale focaccia or brioche
1 pinch cinnamon
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the flour, about 1 cup sugar, about 14 tbsp cold diced butter, 1 whole egg, and 1 yolk in a food processor.

2. Pulse until the dough begins to come together.

3. Transfer to a work surface.

4. Knead briefly.

5. Shape into a ball.

6. Wrap.

7. Rest in a cool place for 1 hour.

8. Put the raisins in a bowl.

9. Add the sweet wine and rum.

10. Soak for at least 30 minutes.

11. Chop the almonds, walnuts, and pine nuts.

12. Finely dice the candied citron and orange peel.

13. Combine the nuts, candied fruit, and grated focaccia in a large bowl.

14. Add the remaining sugar.

15. Add the nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, and salt.

16. Add the raisins with all of their soaking liquid.

17. Mix into an even filling.

18. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

19. Roll the pastry into a large thin rectangle.

20. Shape the filling into a long cylinder down the center.

21. Fold the pastry around the filling.

22. Seal the seam very thoroughly.

23. Coil the filled roll into a spiral with the seam underneath.

24. Put on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

25. Melt the remaining butter.

26. Mix it with the remaining egg yolk.

27. Brush the surface.

28. Bake for about 1 hour.

29. Cool completely.

Service

Slice thinly and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Seal the pastry carefully so the rich moist filling does not escape during the long bake.

26. Cover.

Fried Natisone Valley pastries filled with walnuts, raisins, pine nuts, grappa, and breadcrumbs.

Esse di Raveo

Friulian butter-and-vanilla cookies shaped into their characteristic letter S.

Yield: about 25 cookies

1 large egg, room temperature
7 tbsp softened butter
1/2 cup granulated sugar
1/4 tsp baker's ammonia

2. Beat with the paddle or whisk attachment until soft and creamy.

3. Beat the egg lightly with a fork.

4. Add it gradually to the butter mixture.

5. Let each addition absorb before adding more.

6. Add all of the flour.

7. Mix briefly only until absorbed.

8. Flatten the dough.

9. Wrap in plastic.

10. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

11. Preheat a conventional oven to 340°F.

13. Roll each piece into a rope.
